calls.head: The Islanders can’t afford to cough it up
calls.body: Almost nobody punishes turnovers like the Maple Leafs, and the Islanders give the puck away in bad spots.
calls.call: The Maple Leafs get at least their usual 8.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Toronto 1st for chances off turnovers (8.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: 6.0% of Toronto’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 8.6%.

calls.head: Expect a track meet
calls.body: The Islanders plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Toronto. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 84.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): NY Islanders 10th (82.9), Toronto 6th (84.1)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 87.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 84.1 and a league average of 82.0.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto a 34% chance, and Toronto proved us wrong.

NYI.head: We gave NY Islanders a 66% chance, but Toronto had other ideas.

surprises.head: NY Islanders tried a different line
surprises.body: B. Horvat, K. Palmieri, S. Holmstrom played 7:16 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of NY Islanders’s usual lines.

surprises.head: Toronto couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Toronto’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 7 games.

story.head: The Maple Leafs beat the Islanders
paras: Colton Sissons opened the scoring midway through the first. Easton Cowan scored the winner midway through the first.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
